extra/agent_mcp.txt.title: Adapting MCP tools for the model
note: **Converts MCP's tool schemas into Ollama's tool-calling format.**
- One adapter, any number of tools - sixty would need no more code
- `t.input_schema` is already JSON Schema - nothing hand-written

extra/agent_mcp.txt.anchor: # 2) Discovery: the server tells us what it offers. We wrote no
extra/agent_mcp.txt.title: Asking the server what it offers
note: **The tool list comes from the server, not from your code.**
- No endpoint URLs, query strings, or schemas written by hand

extra/agent_mcp.txt.title: The agent loop
note: **Up to 8 turns of: ask the model, keep whatever it says.**
- An "agent" is just this loop - no framework involved

extra/agent_mcp.txt.title: Running the model's tool calls
note: **No tool calls means the model answered in plain text, so stop.**
- Each tool it names runs via `mcp.call_tool`, results fed back
- `.data` is the hydrated value; `.content` holds raw blocks
- `resolve_placeholders` / `print_trace` come from agent_helpers.py

extra/note_server.txt.title: Minting an unguessable handle
note: **Creates the identifier that replaces a session.**
- High entropy on purpose: handles must not be guessable or enumerable

extra/note_server.txt.title: Resolving and expiring handles
note: **Looks up a handle, rejecting unknown or expired ones.**
- Holding a handle is not authentication - production also binds it to a user

extra/note_server.txt.title: The open_notebook tool
note: **Creates a notebook and hands back its handle as ordinary data.**
- Because it's a normal argument, the model can see and reuse it

extra/note_server.txt.anchor: This is the 2026-07-28 replacement for an implicit session: the server
extra/note_server.txt.title: What open_notebook returns
note: **Stores the notebook with a TTL and returns the handle to the caller.**
- The `note` field tells the model what to do with the handle next

extra/note_server.txt.anchor: def save_note(handle: str, title: str, content: str) -> dict:
extra/note_server.txt.title: The save_note tool
note: **Writes one note into the notebook named by the handle.**
- Re-resolves the handle every call - nothing is remembered between requests

extra/note_server.txt.title: The list_notes tool
note: **Returns the note titles in one notebook, identified by handle.**
- Change one character of the handle later to see the error

extra/note_server.txt.anchor: # A fixed URI that always returns the same shape. Note the exact rule:
extra/note_server.txt.title: Static resource: the catalog
note: **A fixed URI listing open notebooks and how many notes each holds.**
- List results may vary by authorization, never by connection
- No auth in this lab, so ours is the same for everyone

extra/note_server.txt.anchor: # The handle travels in the URI itself, which is the resource-side equivalent
extra/note_server.txt.title: Resource template: one note
note: **A dynamic URI with the handle and title embedded in the path.**
- The resource-side equivalent of passing the handle as an argument
- A missing note raises -32602 (Invalid params)

extra/note_server.txt.title: The summarize_notes prompt
note: **Packages every note in a notebook into one LLM-ready prompt.**
- Tools write data, resources expose it, prompts package it

extra/helpdesk_server.txt.title: The type hint that becomes a schema
note: **`Literal` compiles into a JSON Schema `enum`.**
- The model is shown the only three values it may send
- A constraint in the schema cannot be argued with; one in prose can

extra/helpdesk_server.txt.title: A name and a docstring
note: **Same code as `get_data(a)` - all that changed is what the model is told.**
- The name says what it does; `order_id` says what to put in it
- The `Args:` line becomes a description on the parameter itself

extra/helpdesk_server.txt.title: Telling two tools apart
note: **This is the tool `fetch_info` was - the one the model picked by mistake every time.**
- Two tools taking the same argument need descriptions to be distinguishable
- Before the merge nothing distinguished it from `get_data`, so the model guessed

extra/helpdesk_server.txt.endAnchor: return f"ticket opened on {order_id} with priority {priority}"
extra/helpdesk_server.txt.title: Constraining what the model may send
note: **The `enum` is enforced; the sentence about when to use it is not.**
- "Use only when the customer is reporting a problem" is advice, not a rule
- Put anything that must hold in the schema, not in the prose

extra/math_server.txt.title: Two arithmetic tools
note: **The gateway will expose these as `math_add` and `math_multiply`.**
- Type hints become the JSON Schema that clients discover

extra/gateway.txt.anchor: from note_server import server as note_service
extra/gateway.txt.title: Importing both servers
note: **Brings in the note and math servers as ordinary Python objects.**
- Composing them this way needs no network hop

extra/gateway.txt.title: Creating the gateway
note: **One FastMCP instance fronting both servers on a single endpoint.**

extra/gateway.txt.title: Mounting under namespaces
note: **`namespace=` prefixes every tool name and resource URI from each server.**
- Tools become `notes_save_note`, `math_multiply`, and so on
- Resource URIs are namespaced the same way
